# Real-document DOCX fixtures

Five whole documents that the importer is tested against, kept as binaries
because the bugs they catch live in markup no hand-built fixture produces:
multilevel clause numbering hung off `HeadingN` styles, grouped VML/DrawingML
artwork, Word's built-in table styles, section-level column breaks.

The synthetic python-docx fixtures in `tests/test_docx_import.py` still cover
every individual feature. These cover what real files *combine*.

## Provenance

| File | Origin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `legal-addendum.docx` | Publicly published law-firm GDPR processor-terms template | **Redacted** — see below |
| `sample3.docx` | State of Illinois IITAA accessibility sample document | Metadata scrubbed; the file links to its own source |
| `tables-merged.docx` | [sample-files.com](https://sample-files.com/documents/docx/) sample set | Generated by python-docx; rides Word's built-in table styles |
| `multi-column.docx` | [sample-files.com](https://sample-files.com/documents/docx/) sample set | Multi-column section breaks |
| `long-report.docx` | [sample-files.com](https://sample-files.com/documents/docx/) sample set | ~50 pages, generated TOC, 29 tables |

These are third-party sample documents, included unmodified except for the
redaction described below. They are test inputs, not part of the library:
this repository's MIT licence covers its own code and does not purport to
relicense them. If you are a rights holder and would prefer a document
removed, open an issue and we will replace the fixture.

## The redaction of `legal-addendum.docx`

Every identifying detail was replaced before the file entered any
repository: firm and party names, people, the matter reference, and the
title-page logos (redrawn at identical pixel dimensions so the group
geometry the fixture exists to exercise is unchanged).

The replacements read as plausible firm and person names. That was a
mistake worth not repeating: a realistic invention can collide with a real
firm or a real person, which is the problem redaction exists to avoid. Any
future scrub should use names nobody could mistake for real.

The scrub covers the **whole package**, not the visible text — the first
pass missed exactly that distinction. Also removed: `docProps/custom.xml`
mail-gateway properties, `customXml` SharePoint tenant GUIDs, and an author
Windows path left in image `descr` attributes.

If you add a fixture, audit every part of the zip, not `document.xml` alone:

```bash
python3 -c "import zipfile,sys; z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]); [print(n) for n in z.namelist()]" file.docx
```

## Adding a fixture

A fixture without tests is not done. Assert the *properties the document is
known to have* — its numbering runs unbroken, its logos are group-sized, its
merges survive — never a golden blob nobody can read. Tests live in
`tests/test_docx_real_documents.py`.
